newsitem.title: UK: Clarke rows back from remarks on EMU argument.
newsitem.headline: Clarke rows back from remarks on EMU argument.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Thursday appeared to row back from a remark he made on Wednesday night that people who thought like him were winning the argument inside the ruling Conservative party on economic and monetary union (EMU).
In television and radio interviews on Thursday he insisted he had merely reiterated government policy and that it was the government that had won the argument on the single currency.

BBC radio played a tape of Clarke's comments at an invitation-only gathering of the Conservative Group for Europe at the party conference in Bournemouth, in which he referred to "local difficulties" in the party over a single currency.
"We do win the arguments inside the Conservative party and we shall continue to do so," he said on the tape.

"We do so in the national interest, which we put above all, and because we have a clear idea of what a partnership of nation states should be like and how Britain should have just as big a role in shaping that as the French, the Germans or any other continental nation."
Commenting on the recording on Thursday, Clarke said journalists were trying to stoke up a dead story.
Prime Minister John Major and Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind had made government policy clear in remarks at the conference on Wednesday.
"I was reiterating the government's policy," Clarke said. "The government policy has come under challenge and I thought Malcolm and the prime minister plainly answered that challenge yesterday."
"We settled that yesterday. Today the subject is the economy," he said, referring to his own speech due at around 1120 GMT.
"I also said that I was repeating the government policy on economic and monetary union. We won the arguments. The prime minister has won the argument on the policy."
